summary: After the tail is reset to generation 0 while the delete record holds a higher-generation outcome, _newest_outcome keeps the stale higher-generation outcome, so later settled deletes are never reported complete.
failure_scenario: Delete record holds outcome=(A,3), live=(B,4) and the voice tail file is unreadable or a version-1 tail (the path pinned by tests/integration/test_voice_deletes.py:501). open() -> _restore -> unproven -> _retire(new_id, 0) (lines 1420-1424, 960-971) restarts the binding at generation 0 although the record knows generation 4. The user then deletes (Cc,0) and the companion acknowledges it. acknowledge_forget() -> _newest_outcome() (1008-1010) compares generations numerically across the reset, so outcome stays (A,3) because 3 > 0. Result: pending=() but delete_outcome != (Cc,0), so host_launcher.delete_voice_conversation (line 2822) returns 'pending' for a delete that is settled, and voice_delete_status (2849-2862) reports 'idle' instead of 'complete' because deleted_previous (908) requires outcome[1]+1 == generation. The browser never shows the completed delete while the pending list is empty. Any older outcome with generation >= the reset binding's generation masks every later completion until generations catch up.
evidence: Synthetic reproduction with real VoiceTailWriter and ConversationContextStore in a temp dir (no network): wrote a delete record outcome=(A,3)/live=(B,4) plus a corrupt tail; open() logged refusal malformed and binding=('Cc',0); after request_forget + acknowledge_forget, pending=() outcome=('A',3) deleted_previous=False. Existing tests assert the reset to generation 0 but never the outcome or status that follows. Fix direction: seed the replacement generation above every generation in the record (live, outcome, pending), or compare outcomes by insertion order rather than numeric generation.

summary: The host and local CLIs install no SIGTERM handling, so on the supported Linux deployment target a service stop kills the process without running launcher.close().
failure_scenario: On Linux (stated deployment target in AGENTS.md) the host runs via main() -> asyncio.run(_run_host_cli), which parks on asyncio.Event().wait() (line 3271). Only KeyboardInterrupt (SIGINT) unwinds into the finally at 3275 that awaits launcher.close(); the only other signal hook is SIGBREAK, which exists on Windows and only in qualification mode (3237). A systemd/docker stop sends SIGTERM and Python's default action terminates the process immediately. The ordered close never runs: voice tail final snapshot and writer drain, Hermes task session/run-record settlement, Kokoro worker child, LiveKit verifier, and the evidence writer are not closed, and no CloseStage observations are recorded. Work state is then recovered only by the next start's crash-recovery path, which announces unknown dispatches. launcher.py _run_local_cli/main (490-530) has the same gap.
evidence: Static read of main() (3702-3727), _run_host_cli finally (3275-3329), launcher.main (512-530), and grep for SIGTERM in src (no hits). A stdlib probe of the same asyncio.run/Event().wait()/finally shape showed SIGINT runs the finally (rc 0, CLEANUP_RAN) and SIGTERM does not (rc -15, no output). I did not run the real host on Linux (no providers/credentials), so the effect on specific resources is by inspection.

summary: Remote TLS certificate coverage is checked with a private CPython test helper and exact-match SANs only, so valid wildcard certificates are refused and a stdlib change can break remote startup.
failure_scenario: --remote with a certificate whose subjectAltName is DNS:*.example.net and canonical origin https://host.example.net: _certificate_san_covers_hostname (1045) compares value.lower() == hostname.lower() and never evaluates wildcard labels, so startup fails with 'TLS certificate does not cover canonical origin hostname' for a certificate a browser accepts. The decode uses ssl._ssl._test_decode_cert (1107), a private test-oriented API with no stability guarantee, and it decodes only the first PEM block of the file.
evidence: Static reading of lines 1025-1113. It fails closed, so no security impact; reported as a deployment-compatibility defect. Not executed.

summary: Coverage: read in full src/hermes_realtime/launcher.py, production_observation.py, providers/kokoro.py, integration/voice_tail.py, scripts/qualify_*.py, scripts/generate_natural_work_corpus.py, tests/test_proposal_host_binding.py, tests/test_search_egress_composition.py; read about 45% of host_launcher.py (consent/revoke reservations, close owners, readiness cue, completion policy, composition 2300-2970, CLI 3104-3330, TLS/origin validators, loaders). Tests ran green here (pip-installed deps): test_voice_tail, test_production_observation, test_kokoro, voice sender tests, restart_recall, proposal binding, search egress, local_launcher (1 LiveKit-gated skip). Material gaps: tests/test_launcher.py (3869 lines), test_qualification_checkpoint.py, test_qualification_full_host_*.py, test_browser_self_acceptance.py, test_production_composition.py, test_confirmed_probe_codex.py, test_qualification_full_host_ingress.py were not read line by line; the Windows-only ones (checkpoint, full-host synthetic audio and ingress) are skipped on Linux and unexecuted here. No mutation proofs were run; host_launcher.py lines ~1850-2300 and 2972-3100 (builder argument validation, preflight) were skimmed only.

voice_tail.py: fuzzed 1500 random sequences (updates, evictions, unsettled rows, freeze, ack, review freeze/ack, close targets) at outbox=6 and batch=3; every state the writer would serialize re-parsed through parse_voice_tail with no rejection, so the write-side invariants match the strict parser. Worst-case row, outbox-row and review-row byte costs fit max_voice_tail_bytes (measured 147 and 51 bytes against the 192 and 64 allowances). The clear_voice_history -> _retire sequence is consistent because the store resets its eviction counter. Review-capacity refusal blocks the sender instead of looping.

providers/kokoro.py: fuzzed _split_streaming_text over 3000 random texts with pronunciations (chunks always re-join to the input, no zero-progress loop) and checked per-chunk word timings are contiguous and end at total_samples; the 24 kHz to 48 kHz interpolation indices are correct; pinned assets are size and SHA verified, download is bounded, and the .part file is atomically replaced; synthesize/cancel/close ownership of _operations has no leak or double-delete. A concurrent close during an in-flight worker call could surface AttributeError in the cancelled executor task (it falls through to engine.create on the worker object); cancelled work only, not reported.

launcher.py LocalBrowserLauncher and host close owners: one-shot start, shielded cleanup on start failure, retry of failed close stages, and per-attempt CloseStage records are consistent. LiveKitRoomPeer.connect disconnects itself on failure, so not marking _verifier_connected on a failed connect leaks nothing. production_observation append is nonblocking, never evicts, and enforces rollover stage order. ProactiveCompletionUpdatePolicy's shorter interrupt text does not lose the result because tasks.py records completed_result_reference into context separately. host_launcher delete_voice_conversation restores or releases input, memory receiver and projection reservation on cancellation or timeout in every branch I traced.

Scripts: qualify_full_purge_cleanup.py hardcodes proofClass real_windows_filesystem, but produce_full_purge_v1 goes through storage_process which refuses non-Windows, non-64-bit or optimized Python, so the label cannot be emitted from another platform. generate_natural_work_corpus.py regenerates tests/fixtures/natural_work_intent_cases.json byte-for-byte equal as JSON (100 cases). _load_api_bearer's environment path skips the 32-character check but HermesApiConfig re-validates the bearer (integration/api.py:190).
